q: A nutrient cycle is a repeated pathway of a particular nutrient from the physical environment to living organisms and back to the ______.
e: The definition specifies the cycle returns the nutrient 'back to the environment'.

q: The six main nutrient cycles include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, and ______.
e: Sulphur is listed as the sixth main nutrient cycle.

q: Nitrogen gas constitutes ______ of the atmosphere.
e: The textbook states nitrogen gas makes up 78% of the atmosphere.

q: The enzyme that catalyses the conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonia is called ______.
e: Nitrogenase is the enzyme produced by nitrogen-fixing bacteria for this reaction.

q: Rhizobium forms a mutualistic association with the roots of ______.
e: Rhizobium is specified to associate with legume roots.

q: Ammonification is the process by which decomposers break down organic nitrogen to produce ______.
e: Ammonification releases ammonia (and ammonium ions) from decaying matter.

q: Nitrifying bacteria such as Nitrosomonas convert ammonium ions into ______.
e: Nitrosomonas converts ammonium to nitrites; Nitrobacter converts nitrites to nitrates.
Denitrifying bacteria reduce nitrates to nitrogen gas ($N_2$).

q: Phosphorus is a component of biological molecules such as RNA, DNA, phospholipids, and ______.
e: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is listed as a key molecule containing phosphorus.

q: In the phosphorus cycle, phosphorus is released from rocks through the process of ______.
e: Weathering of phosphate-containing rocks releases phosphorus into the soil.

q: Sulphur is an essential component of many ______ and enzyme cofactors.
e: The textbook states sulphur is part of many proteins and enzyme cofactors.

q: When fossil fuels are burnt, sulphur is released as ______.
e: Burning fossil fuels releases sulphur as $SO_2$, a component of acid rain.
